subject: Key custody models and SLA questions — follow-up
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Lewis <amelia@cardinalht.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Key custody models and SLA questions — follow-up

Hi Amelia — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few concrete asks so we can scope the next steps with security and infra: 

1) Compliance posture you mentioned
   - You said Cardinal HealthTech is completing SOC 2 Type II (in progress) and will need a BAA for HIPAA-protected data — please confirm.
   - You also flagged GDPR residency for EU patient records; we assume US-only for pilot unless you confirm EU scope.

2) Encryption & key custody shortlist (high-level options from our side)
   - Redwood-managed KMS: we manage keys, AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, regular rotation — fastest onboard.
   - Customer-managed KMS (cloud CMK): you keep the CMK in your AWS account and grant Redwood a cross-account decrypt role (no key export).
   - HSM / BYOK via key-wrapping: you hold keys in CloudHSM or on-prem HSM; we accept wrapped keys or REST-wrapped wrapping keys for session encryption.

3) Items we need from you to recommend a path and estimate timelines/costs:
   - Confirm preference: Redwood-managed vs CMK vs HSM/BYOK. If BYOK/HSM, send your security contact and key export policy.
   - SOC 2 status: expected completion date and whether recent Type II report will be available to vendors.
   - Any minimum SLA or encryption-at-rest certification requirements (e.g., FIPS 140-2 HSM).

Attached: redwood_kms_options_v2.pdf (short pros/cons + integration patterns) and our vendor security questionnaire to kick off (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.docx).

Suggested next steps:
- Please loop in your security lead (or reply with answers) — if agreeable, we can schedule a 45-min technical sync next week with our infra engineer and security architect.
- We’ll pre-fill the questionnaire where possible and send a completed draft for your review.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally on the engineering ask once we have your preference.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

Irene — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few quick answers from our side: 

- SOC 2: we have an in-flight Type II audit targeting late Q1 2027; we can share interim evidence and the most recent Type I if that helps.
- HIPAA: yes, we will need a BAA in place for the pilot dataset.
- GDPR: pilot will be US-only; long term we will need EU residency for patient records (TBD after pilot).

On keys: our security team prefers BYOK (we want to retain full key control). We currently use AWS CloudHSM for critical keys and have an existing KMS/CloudHSM setup. We’d like to understand how Redwood would either accept wrapped keys or integrate via cross-account KMS access.

Looping in Sanjay (Sanjay Rao, Head of Security) on this thread — he’ll coordinate the technical ask. Sanjay, can you confirm whether CloudHSM-wrapped keys are acceptable or if we should plan for a CMK cross-account approach?

Thanks,
Amelia

Cardinal HealthTech

Thanks Amelia — great context and helpful to know CloudHSM is already in play. Quick clarifications and proposed agenda for the technical sync: 

Clarifications we’ll bring to the tech sync:
- BYOK modes we support: wrapped key import (you generate & wrap in CloudHSM and send the wrapped key to Redwood for import) OR CMK cross-account decrypt (we request a grant so Redwood can use the CMK to decrypt tokens at runtime; no plaintext key leaves your account).
- For CloudHSM-wrapped imports we will need your key-wrapping policy and whether you permit importing wrapped symmetric keys into our hardened vault; we’ll also confirm whether FIPS 140-2 validation is required on our end.
- Encryption in transit: Redwood uses TLS 1.3 + mutual TLS for service-to-service; we can support client certs if required.

Proposed tech sync (45 min): 
- Introductions (5)
- Customer key model and constraints (10)
- Redwood integration options & security controls (20)
- Next steps & timeline (10)

Ben, can you draft the short tech checklist for the sync (targeting CloudHSM import steps, required IAM roles, expected SLO impact for CMK cross-account flow) and loop Monica for expected implementation ETA if approved?

Amelia/Sanjay — are you available Thursday 11/25 or Monday 11/29 for a 45-min slot? I’ll send a calendar invite once we have a preferred time.

Appreciate it — I’ll pre-fill the questionnaire and share a redlined copy before the sync.

Best,
Irene

Ben / Monica — forwarding the thread above. Customer preference: BYOK via CloudHSM, long-term CMK option possible. Action items: 

1) Ben: please prepare a 1-page tech checklist covering both import-of-wrapped-keys (CloudHSM workflow) and CMK cross-account grants. Include required IAM roles, minimal permissions, and common gotchas (e.g., key policy principal mismatch, replication constraints).

2) Monica: estimate the implementation effort & timeline for an initial POC that accepts wrapped symmetric keys (assume 2 devs, 2 sprints). Also flag any compliance gaps if we accept wrapped keys (FIPS/HSM attestation, audit logging retention).

3) Both: look at the attached draft questionnaire (I pre-filled obvious answers) and mark anything we should not pre-fill. I’ll coordinate the calendar once Amelia/Sanjay confirm availability.

Keep this internal until we have the sync scheduled.

Thanks — Irene
